articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Below $81,000 Late Friday as Ether Follows
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin broke $81,000 on Friday evening and traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET, below the average price U.S. ETF holders paid.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin gave up $81,000 on Friday evening and kept drifting. It traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET, down 1.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The floor held all day. Then it didn't.

During Friday's U.S. session, bitcoin stayed between $81,000 and about $81,940 on Kraken, according to [CryptoWatchDesk](https://cryptowatchdesk.com/news/market-read-23-oct-us-close-dow-falls-bitcoin-81000-floor-ends-81200). The break came between 6:35 and 6:50 p.m. ET, when Binance quotes fell from $81,156 to $80,911, [EconoTimes](https://econotimes.com/Bitcoin-Falls-Below-81-000-After-a-245-Drop-in-15-Minutes-on-Binance-1761735) reported.

## ETF buyers are now underwater

Glassnode data cited by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/23/live-updates-bitcoin-holds-above-usd81-000-as-the-ai-rout-fades-and-oil-climbs) puts the average cost basis of U.S. spot bitcoin ETF holders near $82,313. At Friday night's price, the typical fund buyer sits roughly 1.9% below what they paid. Those funds saw net outflows on both Thursday and Friday.

The rest of the market moved with it. At 11:54 p.m. ET, CoinGecko showed:

- Ether near $2,378, down 1.4%
- Solana near $102.44, down 1.8%
- XRP near $1.29, down 2.5%

## The next marker is Thursday's low

Thursday's low on Kraken was about $80,814, per CryptoWatchDesk. Bitcoin was trading just under that level late Friday.

*Our read: no panic, just a slow leak. The Fed decides on rates Oct. 28.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Finish the Week $301 Million Ahead Despite Two Red Days
articles.excerpt: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $137.9 million on Friday but still took in a net $301.2 million for the week, Farside data shows.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $301.2 million this week, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data shows. That's after investors pulled money on both Thursday and Friday.

Friday's exits came to $137.9 million. That's about a fifth of Thursday's $635.6 million.

## Three green days, two red

- Monday: +$526.7 million
- Tuesday: +$23.2 million
- Wednesday: +$524.8 million
- Thursday: -$635.6 million
- Friday: -$137.9 million

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $110.3 million of Friday's outflows and Fidelity's FBTC for $31.8 million. MSBT was the only fund with new money, at $4.2 million. Every other fund was flat.

Over five days, IBIT still added about $565.7 million. FBTC lost about $116.6 million. Total net inflows since the funds launched stand near $57.25 billion, per Farside.

## The money left as price slipped

The outflows lined up with bitcoin's slide toward the average price ETF holders paid. Glassnode puts that cost basis near $82,313, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/23/live-updates-bitcoin-holds-above-usd81-000-as-the-ai-rout-fades-and-oil-climbs) reported. Bitcoin traded near $80,780 at 11:54 p.m. ET Friday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*Our read: a rough finish to a decent week. The ledger still closed in the black.*

articles.title: Gold Falls Below $4,000 for the First Time Since July as Oil Climbs
articles.excerpt: Spot gold slipped to $3,998.49 on Friday, its first move under $4,000 since mid-July, as oil kept rate-hike bets alive before the Fed meets.
articles.body_md:
Gold lost $4,000 on Friday. Spot gold fell 0.6% to $3,998.49 an ounce by 2:27 p.m. ET, its first trip below that mark since mid-July, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/gold-heads-for-steep-weekly-loss-as-oil-prices-fuel-fed-rate-concerns.html) reported.

The pressure runs through the Fed. Oil near five-month highs keeps inflation fears alive, and traders put a 78% chance on a December rate hike in CME's FedWatch tool, per CNBC. Higher rates make assets that pay no yield, gold and bitcoin among them, harder to hold. Bitcoin slipped below $81,000 the same evening.

## Selling gold to cover stock losses

Jim Wyckoff of American Gold Exchange said margin calls from the tech selloff pushed investors to sell gold and silver. "Heightened inflation concerns suggest that major central banks of the world won't be able to ease monetary policies as quickly as they want to," he said, according to CNBC.

[Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/wall-street-doubts-golds-near-term-strength-main-street-maintains-bullish) put Friday's low at $3,975.10. Late in the session, spot gold sat near $3,995.81, down 0.7%, per [Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/gold-silver-extend-weekly-losses-hormuz-tensions-push-crude-above-116-kitco). The metal fell about 4% on the week, its worst since June.

Silver did worse. It slid about 1% to $53.97, its lowest since November 2025, CNBC said.

## Inflation data lands a day after the Fed

Traders see a 92% chance the Fed holds on Oct. 28, per CNBC. The PCE inflation report, the Fed's preferred gauge, follows on Oct. 29.

articles.title: Iran Says Two Supertankers Hit Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers carrying over 4.5 million barrels hit mines in Hormuz on Friday. No one has confirmed it.
articles.body_md:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday. No independent party has confirmed the claim.

The IRGC Navy said in a statement carried by state agency IRNA that the ships took an "unauthorized route" through the strait, [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-s-revolutionary-guards-say-2-supertankers-hit-naval-mines-in-strait-of-hormuz/4099071) reported. Explosions and fires knocked out both engine rooms, and the crews abandoned the vessels, the statement said. [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2207183) carried the same account.

Neither report named the ships.

## Oil was already running hot

Brent crude traded above $117 a barrel during Friday's session, [Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-10-23/gold-silver-extend-weekly-losses-hormuz-tensions-push-crude-above-116-kitco) reported. Expensive oil feeds inflation fears, and those fears have fed rate-hike bets that weighed on gold and bitcoin this week.

## Tehran's version of the strait

The claim came with a political message. IRGC Navy commander Ali Ozmaei said "America no longer has a place in the Strait of Hormuz," according to [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610233119). The outlet, which opposes Iran's government, also reported his claim that U.S. forces had moved 600 to 700 kilometers away from the strait.

U.S. officials had not publicly responded to the mine claim in the reports reviewed.

*Our read: until someone names the ships, this is Iran's account alone.*

articles.title: OCC Publishes Final GENIUS Act Stablecoin Rule in Federal Register
articles.excerpt: The OCC's final stablecoin rule under the GENIUS Act ran in the Federal Register on Friday and takes effect Jan. 18, 2027.
articles.body_md:
The rulebook for bank-supervised U.S. stablecoins is now official. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's final GENIUS Act rule ran in the [Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21706/implementing-the-guiding-and-establishing-national-innovation-for-us-stablecoins-act-for-the) on Friday and takes effect Jan. 18, 2027.

The OCC [announced the rule](https://occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-92.html) on Oct. 21. Friday's publication starts the clock.

## Who it covers and what it sets

The rule applies to stablecoin issuers under OCC watch, including subsidiaries of national banks and federal savings associations, federal qualified issuers and some foreign issuers. Most of it sits in a new 12 CFR Part 15.

It sets standards for reserve assets, redemption, risk management, custody, audits and supervision, plus capital requirements, according to [OCC Bulletin 2026-50](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html). The release says issuers got more room to manage reserves than in the proposal, while liquidity and diversification limits stay in place.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent welcomed it. "The GENIUS Act marks a watershed moment in American finance, further cementing the United States as the crypto capital of the world," he said in the OCC's release.

## Anti-money-laundering rules come later

Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money-laundering and sanctions requirements are not in this rule. Those will come through a separate rulemaking. The OCC also said it will announce separately when it starts taking applications.

*Our read: issuers now know the test. They still don't know when they can sit for it.*

articles.title: Starknet Community Backs Research Into Becoming a Standalone Post-Quantum Layer 1
articles.excerpt: In a non-binding poll, 93.52% of Starknet voting power supported studying a move to an independent, quantum-resistant layer-1 network. A white paper is next.
articles.body_md:
Starknet's community has signaled strong interest in exploring whether the network should leave its role as an Ethereum layer-2 and become an independent blockchain built to resist quantum computers.

**The vote**

A non-binding Snapshot poll, open to STRK stakers and delegators from Oct. 15 to Oct. 22, ended with 93.52% of voting power in favor and 3,236 votes cast, StarkWare said in a blog post. The Block also reported on the outcome. StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation have formed a working group to research the idea, with a white paper expected in the coming weeks, followed by a detailed proposal and further community votes. No migration has been approved.

**Why the network is considering it**

As a layer-2, Starknet depends on Ethereum for parts of its system, including its bridge and data availability. StarkWare says both rely on elliptic curve cryptography that could be vulnerable to future quantum computers, so Starknet can only become fully quantum-resistant on Ethereum's schedule, which it puts at 2029.

Other parts of Starknet are further along, the company says. Its STARK proofs use hash functions considered post-quantum secure, and its native account abstraction lets user accounts adopt new signature types without a protocol upgrade. StarkWare has set a 2027 target for full quantum security in its roadmap.

**Why it matters**

Quantum risk has moved from a distant concern to an active planning topic across crypto, including for bitcoin and Ethereum. A layer-2 weighing independence over security timelines would be a notable shift, and the debate could shape how other scaling networks approach the issue.

articles.title: Strategists Expect the Fed to Hold Next Week but Keep a December Hike in Play
articles.excerpt: TD Securities and SMBC expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27-28 meeting, then resume hiking in December, as oil and inflation stay high.
articles.body_md:
With the Federal Reserve in its quiet period before the Oct. 27-28 policy meeting, Wall Street strategists are laying out what they expect, and the consensus points to a pause rather than an end to tightening.

**The forecasts**

TD Securities expects the Fed to keep its policy rate at 4.00% next week despite firm inflation and a solid labor market, according to a note summarized by FXStreet on Friday. The firm said a pause would make a December increase more likely, and it expects further hikes in December and March. "Barring an unexpected shock, the December rate hike is all but locked in," the strategists wrote. They also warned that one weak inflation report could prompt markets to price in a larger half-point move.

SMBC's U.S. rates team likewise forecast no change next week and a return to hikes at the Dec. 9 meeting. In its Oct. 23 weekly, SMBC said Chair Kevin Warsh avoids forward guidance, so his description of inflation and financial conditions at the post-meeting press conference will matter most.

The Fed raised rates by a quarter point in September, its first increase in three years, the Associated Press has reported.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Rate hikes raise the return on cash and Treasuries, which can reduce demand for assets that pay no yield, such as bitcoin. Oil near its highest level since April adds to the inflation risk. A hold paired with a hawkish message could weigh on crypto, while any sign the Fed is less worried about prices could support risk assets. Traders will be watching Warsh's tone closely.

articles.title: SEC Puts Tokenization and 'Super Intelligence' on Its 2027 Exam Priority List
articles.excerpt: The SEC's exam division named tokenization and advanced AI, including 'super intelligence,' among its focus areas for fiscal 2027.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission's Division of Examinations released its priorities for fiscal year 2027 on Friday, and two items stand out for crypto and fintech firms: tokenization and advanced artificial intelligence.

**What is on the list**

The SEC said examiners will pay closer attention to risks tied to evolving market infrastructure, naming Treasury clearing reforms and tokenization. The list also includes emerging technologies, specifically "super intelligence" and other advanced tools that could affect market operations, compliance, fraud prevention and investor protection.

Other focus areas include investment advisers' duties to clients, protection of retail investors in complex or illiquid products, private funds and private credit, broker-dealer anti-money laundering compliance, and cybersecurity. The division oversees more than 34,000 registrants, including advisers, broker-dealers and clearing agencies.

"The markets we oversee continue to evolve rapidly, and the examination program must evolve with them," said Keith Cassidy, director of the Division of Examinations. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins called examinations one of the agency's most important tools for promoting compliance.

The SEC stressed that the list is not exhaustive and may change during the year as markets shift. Decrypt also reported on the inclusion of tokenization and AI.

**Why it matters**

Exam priorities do not create new rules, but they signal where regulators will look first. Firms that tokenize stocks, funds or Treasuries, a fast-growing area, can expect more questions about custody, settlement and disclosures. Naming tokenization as an infrastructure topic also shows the SEC treating it as part of mainstream markets rather than a niche experiment.

articles.title: Franklin Templeton Clears Last Step for ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
articles.excerpt: Franklin Templeton registered two Nasdaq ETFs that reinvest stock dividends into bitcoin exposure, with a prospectus listing an Oct. 27 effective date.
articles.body_md:
Franklin Templeton has completed the final regulatory step before launching two exchange-traded funds that channel stock dividends into bitcoin, Bitcoin Magazine reported.

**The filings**

On Oct. 22, the asset manager filed a Form 8-A with the SEC to register shares of the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF for trading on Nasdaq. A prospectus filed the same day lists Oct. 27 as the effective date.

**How they work**

The equity fund, ticker FBEQ, tracks an index of the 500 largest U.S. companies. At the start, the index holds 95% stocks and 5% bitcoin. Instead of buying more shares, each dividend the companies pay is reinvested into bitcoin exposure, so the bitcoin share grows over time.

There are limits. At each quarterly rebalance, a bitcoin weighting above 5% is cut back to 4.5%, and if it tops 20% between rebalances it is trimmed within two business days. The fund does not hold coins directly; it gains exposure through bitcoin exchange-traded products, futures, options or similar instruments. FBEQ's expense ratio is 0.09%, according to the report. The innovation fund applies the same approach to the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies.

**Why it matters**

The products could give mainstream stock investors gradual bitcoin exposure without opening a crypto account or managing a wallet. They add to a growing list of traditional asset managers building bitcoin into familiar fund formats. The prospectus warns that investors can lose money and that bitcoin's volatility may affect the funds' value.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: SoFi Launches an FDIC-Insured Tokenized Deposit Paying 4.40% for Crypto Customers
articles.excerpt: SoFi's new SOFIE token represents a $1 deposit at SoFi Bank, earns a variable 4.40% APY and can be swapped 1:1 into its SoFiUSD stablecoin to buy crypto.
articles.body_md:
SoFi Technologies has launched SoFi Earn, or SOFIE, which the company calls the first tokenized deposit offered to consumers by a U.S. national bank.

**How it works**

According to SoFi's announcement, each SOFIE represents $1 held on deposit at SoFi Bank and earns a variable 4.40% annual percentage yield. Funds are covered by FDIC insurance up to the usual limits. Customers access SOFIE through their SoFi Crypto account and can convert it one-for-one into SoFiUSD, the bank's stablecoin, to buy crypto in the app or send funds to supported external wallets at any hour.

SoFi notes that the interest and FDIC protection apply to SOFIE only. SoFiUSD is not FDIC-insured, and SoFi says SOFIE itself is not a payment stablecoin. The Block reported that the rollout to SoFi's crypto customers should be completed in November.

"We believe your money should keep working for you until the moment you need it," CEO Anthony Noto said in the release.

**Part of a wider push**

SoFi says this is its fifth crypto product in less than a year. It began offering crypto trading in November 2025 and launched SoFiUSD in December 2025. The company says SoFiUSD already settles its card program over Mastercard's network.

**Why it matters**

Most stablecoins do not pay holders interest. Tokenized deposits give banks a way to offer yield on digital dollars inside existing deposit rules, and the launch comes as regulators finalize stablecoin rules under the GENIUS Act. Rates are variable and can change at any time.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Circle Adds Bitcoin-Backed cirBTC and Euro Stablecoin EURC to Its Gateway Service
articles.excerpt: Circle's Gateway now supports cirBTC and EURC alongside USDC, letting businesses hold one balance per asset and access it across several blockchains.
articles.body_md:
Circle has expanded its Gateway service beyond USDC, adding support for Circle Wrapped Bitcoin (cirBTC) and its euro-backed stablecoin EURC, the company said in a blog post on Friday.

**What changes**

Gateway lets developers and businesses hold a single balance for an asset and use it on multiple blockchains, instead of keeping separate pools of funds on each network. Circle says that after a deposit finalizes, the funds can be accessed on other supported chains in under 500 milliseconds, though it notes timing is not guaranteed.

Under the expansion, cirBTC is supported on Arc and Ethereum. EURC works on Arc, Avalanche, Base, Ethereum, Solana and World Chain. Because Circle issues both tokens, it says Gateway can mint them directly on the destination chain rather than relying on a third party's inventory.

Circle also said its Nanopayments feature, which bundles many small payments off-chain and settles them in batches, now supports cirBTC and EURC. The company is pitching this at AI agents and pay-per-use services that make frequent small purchases.

**Fees and scale**

Gateway fees for cirBTC and EURC are waived on Arc at launch. Elsewhere, the fee is 1 basis point for those two assets, while USDC stays at 0.5 basis points. Circle says Gateway has processed more than $10 billion in volume, based on its internal data as of Oct. 23.

**Why it matters**

Liquidity split across many chains is a long-running pain point for exchanges, wallets and payment firms. Bringing bitcoin- and euro-denominated assets into the same system could make it easier to move value where demand appears, and it widens the role of non-dollar tokens in on-chain payments.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Initia Pauses Its Network After Attacker Mints and Bridges Out About $2.7 Million
articles.excerpt: Initia halted its layer-1 chain and rollups on Friday after a bug let an attacker mint tokens and bridge out about $2.7 million, its co-founder said.
articles.body_md:
Initia, a blockchain designed to link a network of interconnected chains, stopped its layer-1 network and rollups on Friday after a security incident, The Block reported.

**What happened**

Co-founder Ezaan Mangalji, known as Zon, said early findings pointed to a previously unknown bug in the network's MoveVM implementation on the Cosmos SDK. The flaw allowed unauthorized minting of tokens, he said, but did not affect the native INIT token. According to his account, the attacker minted and bridged out roughly $2.7 million in AUSD, ETH and USDC before the chain was paused.

Blockchain researcher Spreek had earlier estimated that about $2.6 million had been cashed out, with more funds still moving. Initia said it was working with security teams, validators and exchanges to measure the full scope of the incident and had not confirmed a final loss figure, The Block reported.

**Market reaction**

INIT fell about 14% right after the exploit was first reported, then reversed and was trading about 14% higher on the day, according to The Block.

**Why it matters**

Halting a chain can limit damage, but it also shows how much control validators and core teams can exercise during an emergency, a trade-off users weigh when choosing networks. Bugs in virtual machines and bridges remain one of the biggest risks in crypto, since a single flaw can let an attacker create assets out of thin air and move them to other chains before anyone reacts.

The investigation is ongoing, and figures may change as Initia releases more details.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Netanyahu Says He Has Asked for a Blockchain Plan in Case of Banking Sanctions
articles.excerpt: Israel's prime minister said in a TV interview that he has requested a plan involving blockchain to help the economy withstand possible banking sanctions. No details were given.
articles.body_md:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he has asked for a plan that would use blockchain to help Israel's economy cope with possible economic sanctions, including restrictions on its banks, The Block reported.

**What he said**

In an interview broadcast Friday on Israel's Channel 10, Netanyahu said the country should prepare an economy able to work around sanctions if they come. Asked whether he saw blockchain as one alternative, he said it was and that he had already requested a plan, according to The Block's account of a translated transcript. Ynetnews also reported that he called for preparing an economy that could evade sanctions and named blockchain as one option.

He did not say who would draw up the plan, which networks or digital currencies it might use, or when it could take effect.

**Wider context**

In the same interview, Netanyahu warned that U.S. military aid would not last forever and said Israel must be able to produce more of its own weapons and ammunition. He said he had set aside an additional 400 billion shekels, about $129 billion, for defense over the coming years, The Block reported.

**Why it matters for crypto**

It is unusual for a sitting head of government to describe blockchain as a possible tool against sanctions. Any concrete plan would likely face close scrutiny from regulators and allies, as sanctions enforcement is a major focus for financial authorities. For now, the remarks are a contingency idea rather than an announced policy, and there is no sign of a specific token or system being chosen.

articles.title: Bitcoin Ends a Quiet Friday Near $81,400 as Oil Surge Keeps Traders Cautious
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin spent Friday in a tight range around $81,000 to $82,000, still below the average cost basis of U.S. spot ETF buyers, as oil climbed and the Fed meeting neared.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin closed out the U.S. trading week with one of its calmest sessions in days, holding in a narrow band while oil prices and next week's Federal Reserve meeting dominated the macro picture.

**Where prices stand**

The CME CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index stood near $81,330 late Friday afternoon, roughly flat on the day, according to Investing.com. Its range for the session ran from about $80,990 to $81,950. Hourly data from StatMuse showed a brief push above $82,000 in the morning that faded before midday, with prices near $81,400 by late afternoon. Ether traded around $2,400 late in the day, according to The Block's price ticker.

The quiet followed a week of swings of about $3,000, CoinDesk reported. Bitcoin is still trading below about $82,300, which Glassnode data cited by CoinDesk puts as the average cost basis of U.S. spot bitcoin ETF holders. That level can act as a hurdle when many fund investors are near break-even.

**What is weighing on the market**

Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel, its highest close since April, CNBC reported, as fears of renewed conflict involving Iran grew. Higher energy costs feed inflation concerns at a time when the Fed has already raised rates once this year. Policymakers meet Oct. 27-28, and a hawkish message could pressure risk assets, including crypto.

**Why it matters**

A steady price after a volatile week suggests traders are waiting for clearer signals. ETF flows, oil and the Fed's decision are likely to set the tone for bitcoin's next move.

articles.title: Brent Settles at Highest Since April as Iran Fears Push Stocks Lower
articles.excerpt: Brent crude closed at $116.72 and the Dow fell 1.2% on Friday as fears of a renewed Iran conflict lifted oil, adding to inflation worries before the Fed meets.
articles.body_md:
Rising oil prices weighed on Wall Street on Friday, and the move adds another layer of uncertainty for crypto markets heading into next week's Federal Reserve meeting.

**The close**

Brent crude rose 3.1% to settle at $116.72 a barrel, its highest settlement since April, while U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate gained 3.8% to $103.27, CNBC reported. The gains followed reports that the U.S. and Israel may be preparing renewed strikes on Iran, with Iran saying it is ready to respond. Reuters also pointed to Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia as a source of concern over Middle East supply.

Stocks fell. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16. The S&P 500 lost 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34, according to Reuters. Energy shares rose to a record high, while consumer and financial stocks lagged.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Higher oil prices can keep inflation elevated, which makes it harder for central banks to ease policy. The Fed raised rates in September, and analysts broadly expect it to hold at its Oct. 27-28 meeting while keeping the door open to another increase later. Tighter financial conditions have tended to weigh on speculative assets such as bitcoin.

Bitcoin was little changed on Friday near $81,000 to $82,000, showing less reaction than stocks. Traders will also watch big tech earnings next week, which Reuters noted include Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post Biggest Daily Outflow Since June as Price Holds Near $82,000
articles.excerpt: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $635.6 million on Thursday, undoing Wednesday's inflows, while bitcoin stayed inside its recent range near $82,000.
articles.body_md:
Money flowed back out of U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds on Thursday, reversing a short run of strong buying.

**The numbers**

The funds recorded about $635.6 million in net outflows on Thursday, more than offsetting the roughly $528.4 million that came in on Wednesday, The Block reported. It was the largest single-day exit since June. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $254.1 million of the withdrawals, followed by Fidelity's FBTC at about $217.5 million and the Ark Invest and 21Shares fund at about $109.4 million. Morgan Stanley's fund was the lone gainer, adding about $2.3 million. Even after Thursday, the funds were still up about $442.7 million for the week, and Decrypt noted that the reversal tipped October's flows back into negative territory.

**Where the price stands**

Bitcoin was about $81,970 at 9:49 a.m. ET Friday, up 0.3% on the day, according to Investing.com, still inside the $80,000 to $87,000 band it has held for about a month. Roughly $440 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over the prior 24 hours, mostly bets on higher prices, The Block reported, citing CoinGlass data.

**Why it matters**

ETF flows have become one of the clearest gauges of institutional demand for bitcoin. The outflow came as a sell-off in technology shares spread across global markets, a reminder that bitcoin still tends to trade alongside tech stocks. Traders are watching whether the $80,000 area holds ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Consumer Sentiment Sits Near Record Lows as Inflation Expectations Edge Up
articles.excerpt: Michigan's sentiment index read 48 in late October, with one-year inflation expectations at 4.7%, while factory activity hit a 53-month high.
articles.body_md:
Americans remain deeply gloomy about the economy, and they expect prices to keep climbing, according to fresh data released Friday.

**What the reports showed**

The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index finished October at 48, a hair below September's 48.1 and about 10.4% lower than a year ago, CNBC reported. The Wall Street Journal noted it is the second-lowest reading in the survey's history and the weakest ever recorded heading into a major U.S. election. Shoppers' one-year inflation outlook rose to 4.7% and their five-year outlook to 3.5%.

A separate S&P Global survey showed manufacturing activity running hotter than forecast, with the purchasing managers' index at 56, its highest in 53 months, according to CNBC.

**The Fed angle**

The Federal Reserve meets next week. Markets expect it to leave its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, but futures priced roughly a 70% chance of a quarter-point hike in December, per the CME FedWatch tool cited by CNBC. The 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.99% Friday after slipping below 5% this week as investors sought safety from a tech-stock sell-off.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Rising inflation expectations and strong factory data both give the Fed reasons to keep policy tight, and higher rates tend to weigh on speculative assets like bitcoin. On the other hand, a weak consumer mood could push officials toward caution. Crypto traders are likely to treat next week's Fed statement as the main event.

articles.title: Stocks Slip and Oil Holds Above $100 as Tech Tries to Steady
articles.excerpt: The Dow fell about 1% Friday as Brent crude hovered near $112, while the Nasdaq edged up after its worst day since June.
articles.body_md:
Wall Street was mixed on Friday as climbing energy prices offset an attempted rebound in technology shares.

**The market picture**

By late morning, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 1%, or roughly 541 points, as of 11:12 a.m. ET, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2% and was on track for a second straight weekly loss, the Associated Press reported. The Nasdaq Composite inched higher as chipmakers Nvidia and AMD bounced after Thursday's sell-off, according to Yahoo Finance, which had been the Nasdaq's worst session since June.

**Oil is the pressure point**

Brent crude hovered near $112 a barrel and U.S. crude climbed to about $102, according to Yahoo Finance, holding near five-month highs on worries about rising tensions in the Middle East. Higher fuel costs feed directly into inflation, which complicates the Federal Reserve's job heading into its Oct. 27 to 28 meeting.

**Bonds as a refuge**

Investors have been moving into Treasurys this week. The 10-year yield held just under 5% on Friday, CNBC reported, after Thursday brought its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, driven by concerns over the heavy borrowing tech companies are doing to fund artificial intelligence projects.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Bitcoin has been moving closely with tech stocks, so a calmer Nasdaq offers some relief. But oil-driven inflation fears keep rate-hike odds alive, and that is a headwind for risk assets across the board, digital ones included.

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Speeds Up Fixes for Bugs That AI Can Easily Find
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin Core will now patch 'easily discoverable' flaws across all supported versions right away, instead of holding them under long embargoes.
articles.body_md:
The developers behind Bitcoin Core, the most widely used software for running the Bitcoin network, have changed how they handle security flaws, citing the rise of AI tools that can spot bugs quickly.

**What changed**

Under the updated policy posted on the project's website, a reported vulnerability can now be labeled "easily discoverable," which the policy describes as a flaw that can be found with minimal effort, "such as through a simple LLM prompt." For those cases, the team will ship a fix to every major version it still maintains as soon as possible, together with a public security advisory, rather than waiting through the usual embargo.

The change was proposed by developer Antoine Poinsot on Oct. 16 and merged on Oct. 22, Bitcoin.com News reported. Poinsot acknowledged that faster releases leave less testing time, CoinDesk reported, and not every developer agreed on how far to go.

**What stays the same**

Other bugs still follow severity-based timelines. Low-severity issues are disclosed two weeks after a fixed major release, and medium and high-severity issues two weeks after the last affected release reaches end of life. Critical bugs, such as those that could create coins or split the chain, are still handled case by case.

**Why it matters**

The update does not mean Bitcoin's cryptography has been broken or that a new exploit was found. It reflects a practical shift: if AI can rediscover a flaw in minutes, keeping it secret protects little, so getting patched software to node operators sooner is the safer path.

articles.title: Robinhood Says Bitcoin, Gold and Oil Contracts Are Its Fastest-Growing Prediction Markets
articles.excerpt: A Robinhood executive said price contracts on bitcoin, gold and oil are growing fastest, with some crypto contracts now settling in 15 minutes.
articles.body_md:
Prediction markets on Robinhood are moving beyond sports and elections, with traders increasingly betting on where bitcoin and commodities will trade.

**What the company said**

JB Mackenzie, who runs futures and prediction markets at Robinhood, said at a New York industry conference on Thursday that contracts tied to the prices of bitcoin, crude oil and gold are now the platform's fastest-growing products, CoinDesk reported. Sports remains the largest category. He added that Robinhood's single biggest event contract in September was tied to the Federal Reserve's rate decision.

Crypto contracts have also become much shorter. Mackenzie said they began with weekly windows, moved to daily, and now include 15-minute settlements. Robinhood's own site lists 15-minute contracts on bitcoin, ether, XRP, gold and oil. He likened the very short contracts to same-day options, which can lead to quick losses, CoinDesk reported.

**A growing business**

Robinhood offers these contracts through Kalshi, a federally regulated exchange. Mackenzie said customers who come for event contracts often go on to trade stocks, crypto and options, and some open retirement accounts. Earlier this week, CEO Vlad Tenev said the unit traded about 2.5 billion contracts in October, more than in the entire third quarter, Startup Fortune reported, citing Yahoo Finance.

**Why it matters**

The growth shows mainstream demand for simple ways to take a view on crypto prices. It also brings more retail activity into regulated venues, though very short-dated contracts carry real risk for inexperienced traders.

articles.title: Phantom Wallet Brings Kalshi Prediction Markets to U.S. Users
articles.excerpt: Self-custody wallet Phantom is rolling out Kalshi's regulated prediction markets to U.S. users, using CFTC no-action relief it secured in March.
articles.body_md:
Phantom, one of the most popular self-custody crypto wallets, has started offering regulated prediction markets to users in the United States.

**How it works**

In a company blog post Friday, Phantom said U.S. access will expand over the next few weeks through its first U.S. integration with Kalshi, a CFTC-registered exchange. Users verify their identity inside the app through a third-party service. Kalshi then approves and holds their trading accounts and executes trades sent from Phantom.

**The regulatory groundwork**

Phantom said it asked the Commodity Futures Trading Commission earlier this year whether a non-custodial app could connect people to a registered exchange without registering as an introducing broker. In March, CFTC staff issued a no-action letter saying it would not need to, under certain conditions, and in September the agency extended similar relief to comparable software providers.

Kalshi welcomed the launch. "Phantom did the regulatory work up front, and it's a model for how prediction markets can reach more people," Max Crowley, Kalshi's vice president of business development, said in Phantom's announcement.

The rollout comes as several states challenge prediction markets in court, The Block reported, though Phantom said it is comfortable proceeding.

**Why it matters**

The launch is a notable step for self-custody wallets, which have often been limited in the regulated products they can offer. It also extends the reach of prediction markets, one of the fastest-growing corners of crypto-linked trading.

articles.title: Malaysia and Thailand Join Singapore's Cross-Border Stablecoin Project
articles.excerpt: The central banks of Malaysia and Thailand joined Singapore's BLOOM initiative, which works on cross-border settlement with stablecoins and tokenized deposits.
articles.body_md:
Three Southeast Asian central banks are now working together on how digital money can move between their countries.

**What was announced**

The Monetary Authority of Singapore said Friday that Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand have joined its BLOOM initiative as policymaker members, The Business Times reported. BLOOM, launched by Singapore last October, brings together regulators, banks, payment networks and technology firms to explore cross-border use of regulated stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits.

The group will focus on three areas: how digital money is accepted and settled across borders, how different digital money systems can work together, and built-in safeguards such as identity checks, sanctions screening and transaction controls.

"As financial institutions and jurisdictions develop different digital money use cases, including for tokenised deposits and regulated stablecoins, greater coordination will be important to support its effective use across borders," MAS said, according to The Business Times.

**Who is involved**

Industry participants include DBS, OCBC, UOB, Standard Chartered, JPMorgan, Coinbase, Circle and StraitsX, along with later additions such as Visa, Mastercard, Ripple, Maybank, Airwallex and the World Bank Group. Ripple said in March it would test trade payments using its RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger through the program, The Block reported.

**Why it matters**

Central bank backing gives regulated stablecoins a clearer path into everyday cross-border finance in a fast-growing region. For issuers like Circle and Ripple, it could open new payment corridors under official oversight.

articles.title: USDT Is Headed Back to Bitcoin, With a Public Launch Set for Nov. 28
articles.excerpt: Utexo opened early testing for USDT on Bitcoin via the RGB protocol, with a public launch planned for Nov. 28 and Lightning support in early 2027.
articles.body_md:
The world's largest stablecoin is preparing to return to the Bitcoin network, where it first launched in 2014.

**What's happening**

Utexo has opened Utexo Mint, a platform where verified exchanges, wallets, market makers and other professional operators can test minting, private transfers and redemption of USDT on Bitcoin, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Testing runs in a sandbox ahead of a public launch scheduled for Nov. 28, when USDT is set to become available on Bitcoin through partner wallets and exchanges.

The token uses RGB, a protocol that keeps transaction details off the public chain. A second phase, planned for the first quarter of 2027, would extend USDT to the Lightning Network for payments.

**Who is behind it**

Utexo, not Tether, is launching the product, and Tether does not own or operate Utexo Mint, according to Bitcoin Magazine. The Bitcoin version is backed by USDT through Tether's USDT0 system, with the backing held on Arbitrum, The Defiant reported. Utexo said it screens incoming funds with anti-money-laundering checks and works with Crystal Intelligence on risk monitoring, KuCoin News reported.

**Why it matters**

Dollar stablecoins have mostly lived on other blockchains. Bringing USDT back to Bitcoin could add dollar liquidity for trading and bitcoin-backed lending directly on the network, and Lightning support could make it useful for payments. As with any new bridge-based product, adoption and security in practice will be worth watching after launch.

articles.title: New York Seeks Nearly $1.37 Billion From NovaTech Founders Who Fled the U.S.
articles.excerpt: New York's attorney general is asking a court for about $1.37 billion from the founders of NovaTech, an alleged crypto pyramid scheme.
articles.body_md:
New York's attorney general is pressing for one of the largest recoveries yet in a crypto fraud case aimed at everyday investors.

**What the state is asking for**

In a court filing Thursday, Attorney General Letitia James sought about $1.13 billion in disgorgement plus roughly $232.5 million in interest, nearly $1.37 billion in total, from NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion, The Block reported. The court entered a default judgment against the couple in August 2025 after they did not respond to the lawsuit, and the attorney general's office says they have since left the country.

**The allegations**

According to the filing, investors deposited about $1.16 billion in crypto into NovaTech's wallet between August 2019 and May 2023, and at least $134.5 million in withdrawals went to wallets belonging to the founders. Only about $26 million was sent to a trading platform provider over a similar period. Prosecutors allege that the so-called trading profits and recruiting bonuses were paid with money from newer investors.

James first sued NovaTech and crypto mining firm AWS Mining in June 2024, calling both pyramid schemes. Her office has said the schemes targeted immigrant and religious communities. Four promoters agreed to pay nearly $6 million and accepted permanent bans from the securities, commodities and crypto industries.

**Why it matters**

The case is a sobering reminder that promises of steady, guaranteed crypto returns are a classic warning sign. Recovering money from founders who have left the country will be difficult, but the judgment could help victims pursue claims.

articles.title: Interpol Sweep Across Africa Recovers $105 Million and Shuts Illegal Crypto Mines
articles.excerpt: Operation Serengeti III led to 1,462 arrests in 21 countries, recovered over $105 million and dismantled two illegal crypto mining centers in Angola.
articles.body_md:
One of Africa's largest cybercrime crackdowns has wrapped up with more than 1,400 arrests and over $105 million recovered, Interpol said this week.

**The operation**

Police from 21 countries took part in Operation Serengeti III between June 29 and Aug. 31, Interpol said in a statement on Oct. 22. They arrested 1,462 suspects, disrupted 10,909 malicious networks and identified nearly 66,000 victims. Investigators tied the networks to losses of more than $385 million from scams, ransomware, business email compromise and online extortion.

**The crypto angle**

In Angola, authorities shut down two illegal cryptocurrency mining centers, arrested nine people and seized more than 2,000 mining machines along with six illegal power stations; the electrical equipment alone was valued at over $1 million. In Nigeria, one investigation tracked more than $2.4 million in suspected criminal proceeds, much of it laundered through cryptocurrency. Uganda's police broke up two fraud rings that used fake trading platforms to target pensioners.

"Cybercrime networks operate without regard for borders, exploiting technology to target victims on an unprecedented scale," said Neal Jetton, Interpol's director of cybercrime.

**Why it matters**

Illegal mining and crypto-based laundering hurt legitimate users and give the industry a bad name. Coordinated action across borders, supported by private security firms, shows that crypto's public ledgers can help investigators follow the money and protect people from fraud.

articles.title: Bitcoin Settles Into a Quiet Range as Traders Wait on Next Week's Fed Decision
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin has moved less than 6% in a month. Analysts call the calm a possible setup for a bigger move, with the Fed's Oct. 28 decision as the next test.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin is trading in an unusually narrow band, and some analysts see that as a sign of strength rather than weakness.

**Where prices stand**

Bitcoin was near $81,735, down 1.2% on the day, in Decrypt's report early Friday. Decrypt's data show it has not moved more than 6% over the past month, and none of the five largest cryptocurrencies has moved more than 2% over the past week. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index sat at a neutral 47.

**Why some see the calm as constructive**

André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, described the period as one of staying power more than excitement, noting that bitcoin's pullbacks in this recovery have been shallower than in past cycles even as oil, chip stocks and bonds swing sharply. Jake Koch-Gallup of Blockworks said similar low-volatility stretches have historically been followed by 30% moves in either direction within a few months.

Not everyone reads it the same way. Carlos Guzman of GSR said a broad risk-off mood, driven largely by macro worries and doubts about AI stocks, is keeping crypto stuck, and that buying has been too uneven to power a lasting rally.

**What comes next**

Analysts pointed to three near-term events: the Federal Reserve's rate decision on Oct. 28, a large bitcoin options expiry on Oct. 30, and the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. Koch-Gallup said a steady Fed plus continued ETF inflows could favor an upward break, while another hike could bring the $75,000 to $77,000 area back into focus.

**Why it matters**

With the Fed having raised rates in September, the next decision is the clearest near-term driver for bitcoin and other risk assets.

articles.title: HSBC Launches RedCoin, Its First Hong Kong Dollar Stablecoin, for Retail Users
articles.excerpt: HSBC's RedCoin goes live on its PayMe app, letting users send Hong Kong dollar stablecoins to friends and pay more than 100,000 merchants.
articles.body_md:
HSBC has brought a bank-issued stablecoin to everyday users in Hong Kong.

**What launched**

The bank's first Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin (RCHKD), became available on its PayMe platform on Friday, The Block reported. In the coming days, users will be able to turn on a stablecoin wallet inside the app and use it for person-to-person transfers and for payments at more than 100,000 PayMe merchants.

Maggie Ng, HSBC's chief executive for Hong Kong, said money, assets and information are moving onto digital networks that run around the clock and are becoming more programmable. John O'Neill, the bank's managing director for digital assets and currencies, said more products are planned, including uses for corporate and institutional clients.

**How it fits in**

HSBC is one of three commercial banks authorized to issue Hong Kong dollar banknotes. Hong Kong's Stablecoins Ordinance took effect in August 2025, creating a licensing system for issuers, and in April 2026 the Hong Kong Monetary Authority granted its first stablecoin licenses to HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial, a venture of Standard Chartered, HKT and Animoca Brands. HSBC also runs a gold token for retail clients and a tokenized deposit service for wholesale payments.

**Why it matters for crypto**

A major global bank putting a regulated stablecoin in front of retail customers is a meaningful adoption step. It also shows non-dollar stablecoins growing under clear local rules, which could broaden how digital money is used for daily payments in Asia.

articles.title: South Korea Plans Forex Law Change to Treat Stablecoins as Payment Instruments
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Korea says it will work with the government on a bill this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, as a broader crypto law nears completion.
articles.body_md:
South Korea is moving to write stablecoins into its foreign exchange rules.

**The plan**

The Bank of Korea and the government intend to amend the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act this year so stablecoins are regulated as payment instruments, The Block reported, citing local outlet Digital Asset. The central bank said it plans to prepare the bill jointly with the government, along with a framework for monitoring virtual assets and cross-border digital asset transactions.

The step follows a National Assembly audit last year in which lawmakers asked the central bank to bring local payment infrastructure up to global standards and to guard against money laundering risks as global crypto exchanges enter the market.

**Concerns the central bank raised**

The Bank of Korea noted that crypto lets money move across borders outside traditional banks, and that tools such as mixers and unhosted wallets can add anonymity. It said it will build international cooperation against illegal digital asset activity.

**The bigger picture**

Separately, the government is drafting the Digital Asset Basic Act, a broad framework that would include licensing for exchanges and rules for stablecoin issuance. Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon said Thursday that discussions on that bill were nearly finished and that the government aims to introduce it as soon as possible.

**Why it matters for crypto**

South Korea has one of the world's most active retail crypto markets. Clear legal status for stablecoins could open the door to regulated won-based tokens and cross-border payment uses, while giving authorities tighter oversight of capital flows.

articles.title: Sweden's Central Bank Urges Lawmakers to Revisit a Digital Krona
articles.excerpt: The Riksbank warns foreign-currency stablecoins and a future digital euro could weaken the krona's role in payments and wants legislative work to start now.
articles.body_md:
Sweden's central bank wants lawmakers to take another look at a digital version of the krona.

**What the Riksbank is saying**

The Riksbank is concerned that stablecoins tied to foreign currencies, along with a planned digital euro, could erode demand for the krona over time, CoinDesk reported. It sees little near-term risk but says the long-term threat is real.

Deputy Governor Per Jansson warned that if payments go fully digital and the krona has no practical digital form, it could lose out to easier-to-use digital options that move freely across borders, according to Reuters as cited by CoinDesk.

**Background**

A 2023 government inquiry found too little need for an e-krona. The Riksbank says changes in how people pay and rising security risks justify a fresh review. Only 5% of Swedes surveyed used cash for their most recent purchase, according to Riksbank data cited in the report. The bank also sees an e-krona as a backup for payments during power or telecom outages, possibly with offline features.

The Riksbank has not decided whether to issue one. It wants legislation prepared now because the work would take at least five years. Sweden could build on digital euro infrastructure, which might debut in 2029 if EU lawmakers approve the rules.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The debate shows how quickly stablecoins have become a policy concern for central banks. As private digital dollars spread, more countries may push their own digital currencies, shaping the competition stablecoin issuers face in Europe.

articles.title: Ethereum Developers Postpone Glamsterdam Testnet Upgrade After Security Review
articles.excerpt: Developers called off Monday's Glamsterdam activation on the Hoodi testnet after auditors found proposed gas changes could alter how existing contracts handle failures.
articles.body_md:
Ethereum's next major upgrade is taking a pause after security researchers flagged a potential problem.

**What happened**

Developers postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi test network, which had been set to activate on Oct. 26, CoinDesk reported. The decision came during Thursday's All Core Devs Execution call. A planned increase of Hoodi's gas limit to 200 million was also put on hold, and no new date has been set.

**The concern**

Security firm ChainSecurity published research on Oct. 13 showing that two proposals, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, could change how existing smart contracts behave when an operation they call runs out of gas. Some contracts rely on a failed step reversing the whole transaction. Under the new gas rules, some contracts could end up with more gas than expected, allowing a failure to be recorded permanently, or with less, causing valid operations to fail. In one example, creating a new storage slot could cost 110,020 gas versus 22,100 under current rules.

CoinDesk noted that ChainSecurity has shown how the issue could arise but has not shown that any major live protocol is exploitable, and there is no sign of current exploitation.

**Context**

Glamsterdam includes a new system for choosing block builders and changes meant to support larger blocks. It went live on the Sepolia testnet on Oct. 6. Mainnet timing remains unconfirmed.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The delay may push back Ethereum's scaling plans, but catching compatibility risks on a testnet, before mainnet, is the purpose of the testing process.

articles.title: CoinDCX Denies New Hack After $16 Million Moves From Old Wallet Addresses
articles.excerpt: India's largest exchange says $16 million in flagged outflows came from addresses compromised in 2025, while investigator ZachXBT disputes that they were fully retired.
articles.body_md:
India's largest crypto exchange is pushing back on reports of a fresh security breach.

**What was flagged**

On Wednesday, an X user named Darcy pointed to about $16 million in USDT and TRX leaving CoinDCX's hot wallet and several of its deposit addresses, all sent to a single Tron address and then split up, CoinDesk reported. The largest transfer was about 15.8 million USDT.

**CoinDCX's response**

A CoinDCX spokesperson said the activity involved old addresses created in January 2025 and compromised in a July 2025 attack, which cost the exchange about $44 million. The spokesperson said the exchange's current main and user addresses were unaffected and that no funds in active wallets had been compromised, CoinDesk reported. CEO Sumit Gupta called it a false alarm on X.

**The dispute**

On-chain investigator ZachXBT challenged that account, saying at least one of the addresses was used by a liquidity provider for 10 months after the 2025 incident and passed deposits to CoinDCX's current hot wallet as recently as April and May 2026.

CoinDCX said some users kept depositing to retired addresses despite warnings, and a temporary failure in its process for sweeping those deposits caused operational losses that it absorbed after crediting affected users. It said customer assets are held in cold wallets and trading continues normally.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The episode is a reminder that old deposit addresses can remain a risk long after a hack, and that exchanges face close public scrutiny of their wallet practices.

articles.title: Brent Crude Hits Five-Month High as Mideast Tensions Weigh on Markets
articles.excerpt: Brent touched $114.72 on Friday amid Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, keeping inflation worries alive ahead of next week's Fed decision.
articles.body_md:
Oil prices climbed again Friday, adding to the inflation concerns hanging over markets.

**The numbers**

Brent crude futures rose 79 cents to $113.96 a barrel by 08:10 GMT (4:10 a.m. ET), after earlier touching $114.72, the highest since May 4, Reuters reported via Yahoo Finance. U.S. West Texas Intermediate gained $1.10 to $100.57. Brent is on track for a third straight weekly gain of almost 4%.

**What is driving it**

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised fears of further supply disruption. Reuters reported that Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters on Thursday as fighting intensified. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said traders remain worried that an escalation could, in the worst case, disrupt supply again. A pipeline shutdown in Libya also cut output at two fields.

**Stocks**

U.S. stock futures were mixed early Friday after Thursday's steep tech selloff. Dow and S&P 500 futures were down about 0.2%, while Nasdaq 100 futures were little changed, Yahoo Finance reported.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Higher energy prices can keep inflation elevated, which makes it harder for the Federal Reserve to ease and tends to pressure risk assets such as bitcoin. The Fed's Oct. 28 decision is the next key event, and analysts have pointed to Middle East tensions as one of the factors that could either weigh on or lift crypto markets depending on how they unfold.

articles.title: Senate Democrat Seeks Answers on Tether Payments to Bo Hines' Consulting Firm
articles.excerpt: Sen. Richard Blumenthal sent letters to Tether and Nxum over reported payments made while Hines advised the White House. Tether says an outside review found no wrongdoing.
articles.body_md:
Tether faces another round of questions from Capitol Hill.

**The inquiry**

Sen. Richard Blumenthal, the top Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, sent letters Thursday to Tether and to Nxum Group, a consulting firm co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines, CoinDesk reported. Hines now leads Tether's U.S. business.

The letters follow a Wall Street Journal report that Nxum received large consulting payments from Tether while Hines was still advising the administration on crypto policy, including stablecoin rules. Blumenthal asked for details of those arrangements, saying their terms raise serious ethical and legal questions.

**Tether's response**

Tether said in a statement that an earlier internal investigation led by outside lawyers found no evidence of wrongdoing. CEO Paolo Ardoino had criticized Blumenthal's work earlier this week, saying the senator overlooked important information.

**Context**

Blumenthal has been probing several crypto matters, including Tether's ties to Cantor Fitzgerald. Because his party is in the minority, his powers are limited, but CoinDesk noted that a Democratic Senate win in November would likely make him subcommittee chair with subpoena power. Prediction market Kalshi put Democrats' chances of taking the Senate at 69% at the time of CoinDesk's report.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Tether issues the largest stablecoin. Political scrutiny of its U.S. dealings could shape how stablecoin rules are enforced, especially if control of Congress shifts after the midterms.

articles.title: Polymarket Reportedly Fires Marketing Chief as It Eyes a Possible IPO
articles.excerpt: The New York Post reports Polymarket ousted CMO Matthew Modabber after an internal probe, as the prediction market works to polish its image ahead of a possible IPO.
articles.body_md:
Polymarket has parted ways with its chief marketing officer, according to a New York Post report cited by CoinDesk.

**What was reported**

Matthew Modabber, a longtime friend of CEO Shayne Coplan who had served as CMO since January 2024, was let go after an internal investigation into several incidents, the Post said, citing unnamed sources. One source said a separation agreement was being finalized. Polymarket's board reportedly concluded he was getting in the way of the company's effort to move past its startup image as it considers a potential initial public offering.

**Earlier allegations**

One episode drew attention in June, when The Wall Street Journal reported that Modabber's team built a webpage showing videos of users profiting from fake trades. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission opened an investigation that is still ongoing, and no wrongdoing has been proven. At the time, Polymarket said it was committed to running accurate, fair and transparent markets.

The Post reported that Coplan initially resisted the move before accepting it was best for the company. The board includes Coplan, investor Nick Tomaino, lawyer Alex Spiro and a partner at Founders Fund.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Polymarket is one of crypto's most visible consumer apps. How it handles governance and regulatory questions will matter for its IPO hopes and for how regulators and investors view blockchain-based prediction markets more broadly.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Cardano Treasury Proposal Would Put About $5 Million Into Tokenized Copper
articles.excerpt: Toto Finance is asking Cardano's treasury for 22 million ADA to build a tokenized copper reserve. Voting closes Nov. 15.
articles.body_md:
Cardano's on-chain treasury is weighing an unusual real-world asset proposal.

**The proposal**

Toto Finance, which turns physical commodities into blockchain tokens, is requesting 22 million ADA, roughly $5 million, for what it calls the Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve, CoinDesk reported. Voting closes Nov. 15.

About two-thirds of the funds would buy exchange-grade copper stored in a COMEX-approved warehouse near New Orleans, with a token called CuTT representing each verified pound. The copper would be held for 18 to 24 months, then sold over the following year, with proceeds and unused funds returned to the treasury by month 36. The remaining third would cover storage, insurance, audits, oversight and Toto's work.

**The math**

If the full budget is spent and ADA's dollar price is unchanged, copper would need to rise about 49.4% for the treasury to break even, according to CoinDesk's analysis. Toto could receive up to about 3.36 million ADA in fees and margins, roughly 15% of the request, and would keep commercial rights to its CuTT business.

Founder Monty Metzger said bullish forecasts could clear that hurdle but acknowledged that commodity prices can fall, and he said Toto would not profit from the proposal, according to CoinDesk. The tokens would first be minted on Ethereum and bridged to Cardano, and the contracts and security reviews are still to be completed.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The vote is a test of how a community-governed treasury weighs tokenized real-world assets against risk, cost and the use of its limited withdrawal budget.

articles.title: Bitcoin Climbs Back Toward $82,000 in Asian Trading as Yen Rally Fades
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin recovered from an overnight dip below $81,000 as Asian stocks and gold bounced, though ETF outflows and $100 oil remain headwinds.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin found its footing early Friday in Asia after Thursday's slide.

**Where prices stand**

Bitcoin climbed back to nearly $82,000 after trading below $81,000 overnight, CoinDesk reported at 11:13 p.m. ET Thursday. At that point it was testing its 50-day simple moving average, a common gauge of short-term momentum. Ether, XRP, solana and dogecoin moved in a similar pattern.

**What changed overnight**

The early mood in Asia was cautious. The Japanese yen strengthened to 156.07 per dollar, its strongest level since Sept. 18, after hotter-than-expected Japanese inflation data added to expectations of more Bank of Japan rate hikes. A stronger yen can pressure risk assets because the currency is widely borrowed to fund trades elsewhere.

That move did not last. The yen slipped back toward 157, and Japan's Nikkei, South Korea's Kospi and Nasdaq futures recovered from their session lows. Gold also bounced to about $4,020 an ounce from an early low of $3,986, according to CoinDesk.

**The headwinds**

About $435 million in crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $385 million in bullish bets, a sign that leverage had leaned toward buyers. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw $381 million in outflows Thursday, according to preliminary SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk, a reversal after more than $1 billion of inflows earlier in the week.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Oil remains a key variable. WTI crude was trading near $100 even after a new White House push to raise U.S. fuel output. Persistent energy-driven inflation could keep interest rates higher, which tends to weigh on bitcoin and other risk assets.

articles.title: Solana's Alpenglow Upgrade Goes Live, Cutting Finality to About 150 Milliseconds
articles.excerpt: Solana replaced its original consensus system on mainnet, aiming to make transactions final in about 150 milliseconds instead of roughly 12.8 seconds.
articles.body_md:
Solana has completed the largest change to its core protocol since the network launched in 2020.

**What happened**

The Alpenglow consensus upgrade activated on mainnet at the start of epoch 1064 on Wednesday, Oct. 21, according to the Solana Foundation. Validators kept running the old system, TowerBFT, for about 5,000 slots before the new protocol took over at slot 459,653,000. The Solana Foundation said the handoff took about 900 milliseconds, with 446 of 654 participating validators voting to certify the starting block.

Anza, the engineering firm that built Alpenglow, said finality, the point at which a transaction can no longer be reversed, drops from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds. CoinDesk noted that 150 milliseconds is a target under normal network conditions rather than a guarantee for every payment.

**How it works**

Under the old design, validators voted by sending transactions on the chain. With Alpenglow's voting protocol, called Votor, they send votes directly to one another and bundle them into certificates, so a block can be final after one or two voting rounds. A second piece, Rotor, which will change how block data spreads across the network, is planned but not yet scheduled.

**What users notice**

Wallets, apps and fees stay the same. CoinDesk pointed out one side effect: because validator votes are no longer recorded as transactions, dashboards that counted them will show lower transaction totals even if real user activity is unchanged.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Faster, near-instant settlement is aimed at exchanges, merchants and financial firms that wait for finality before treating money as moved. CoinDesk reported SOL fell 2.4% to around $104 on Thursday morning amid a broad market dip, so the upgrade has not yet shown up in price.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: a16z Renames Its Crypto Arm 'a16z Frontier' and Widens Its Focus to AI and Robotics
articles.excerpt: Andreessen Horowitz is renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier, adding AI and robotics while saying it will keep investing in crypto.
articles.body_md:
One of crypto's best-known venture investors is changing its name and broadening its scope.

**What happened**

Andreessen Horowitz said Thursday it is renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier. In a blog post, managing partner Chris Dixon said the new fund will back "frontier" startups building technologies and markets that may take years to develop, including artificial intelligence, robotics and new kinds of networks.

Dixon stressed that the firm is not walking away from digital assets. "This is an expansion: we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation," he wrote.

He argued that as blockchains are used more widely, the label matters less. Wall Street and fintech firms now regularly launch products built on blockchains, he said, so it makes more sense to define companies by what they do than by the technology underneath.

**Who is involved**

Dixon will lead the fund with a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz and general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Fortune reported that the change widens the scope of a $2.2 billion fund announced in May. TechCrunch reported the unit has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds since 2018, with past bets including Coinbase.

**Why it matters for crypto**

The move can be read two ways. TechCrunch framed it as a sign that crypto-only investing has lost some of its pull with venture firms. Dixon's own framing is that blockchain technology is becoming ordinary infrastructure inside wider tech. Either way, the shift suggests crypto startups may increasingly compete with AI and other emerging fields for the same pool of venture money.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Chainlink Teams Up With LG CNS to Build Out Korea's Digital Asset Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: LG Group's tech arm will add Chainlink's cross-chain and data tools to its digital asset platforms and work on expanding Korean won stablecoins.
articles.body_md:
Chainlink has landed a partnership with one of South Korea's largest corporate groups.

**What happened**

Chainlink announced a strategic partnership with LG CNS, the IT services and AI arm of LG Group, The Block reported Thursday. LG CNS will build Chainlink's cross-chain, data and orchestration tools into the digital asset platforms it offers to Korean institutions.

The two companies also said they will work on expanding the use and distribution of Korean stablecoins, a segment The Block described as having more than 11 million eligible users, and on helping develop the country's digital asset framework.

"Korea's financial infrastructure is entering the tokenization era," said Hongkeun Kim, executive vice president and head of the digital business division at LG CNS, according to the announcement. He said the partnership aims to speed up the growth of Korea's tokenized securities market.

**The backdrop**

South Korea does not yet have a clear legal basis for issuing and trading stablecoins tied to the won. Lawmakers and the government are working on the Digital Asset Basic Act, which would set rules for won stablecoins and other parts of the market, according to The Block.

LG CNS is also the lead contractor for the Bank of Korea's digital currency effort, Project Hangang. The announcement did not say Chainlink would be part of that project.

**Why it matters for crypto**

Korea is one of the world's most active crypto markets, which The Block put at about $68 billion. A tie-up with a major conglomerate's tech arm gives Chainlink a foothold with Korean institutions as the country moves toward formal rules for stablecoins and tokenized assets. The Block's market ticker showed LINK near $12.12 late Thursday.
